title: Coconut custard tart
subtitle: a sweet pastry case filled with a rich coconut milk custard, baked until set
excerpt: Coconut custard tart has a sweet pastry shell filled with a baked custard made from coconut milk and cream, set with eggs and egg yolks. The coconut milk gives the custard a gentle tropical sweetness and a smooth, silky texture. The tart is baked low and slow and has a creamy, wobbling set when it comes out of the oven.
sourceNotes: Coconut custard tarts draw on both European patisserie tradition and South-East Asian coconut dessert traditions. The combination of coconut milk with an egg-based baked custard is found in Thai and Malaysian sweets, adapted into a Western tart format in the British restaurant scene from the 1990s onward.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made the day before and refrigerated overnight. Remove from the fridge 30 minutes before serving.
recipe.temperatureNote: fan 130 degrees C / gas 2 for the custard filling

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: fan 130 degrees C / gas 2 for the custard filling

content.text: Coconut custard tart is a crisp sweet pastry case filled with a coconut milk and cream custard, set firm by baking at a low temperature without a water bath. The coconut milk is rich enough to carry the custard without cream on its own, but a little double cream gives the filling extra body. The custard bakes to a pale cream with a gentle wobble that firms as it cools.

Make, rest, and blind-bake the pastry in a 23 cm tart tin at 200 degrees C (fan 180 degrees C / gas 6): 15 minutes with beans, then 8 minutes without, until pale golden and dry. Cool. Reduce the oven to 150 degrees C (fan 130 degrees C / gas 2).
Whisk the eggs, egg yolks, and caster sugar together until just combined. Add the vanilla. Stir in the coconut milk and double cream. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve into a jug.

Place the blind-baked tart case on a baking sheet. Pull the oven shelf out slightly and place the tart on it. Pour the custard carefully into the shell, filling it to just below the rim. Gently push the shelf back.
Bake for 35 to 45 minutes until the custard is set at the edges but still has a gentle wobble across the centre. The surface should be barely coloured.
Leave to cool in the tin on a rack for 1 hour, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours until fully chilled and set. Scatter toasted desiccated coconut over the surface before serving if using.

attrs.problem: Custard developing a thick, tough skin on top
attrs.avoid: Avoid too high an oven temperature; a skin forms when the surface dries out in a hot oven.
attrs.fix: The 150 degrees C temperature is the ceiling for this filling. If the oven runs hot, reduce by 10 degrees and extend the baking time accordingly.

attrs.problem: Custard leaking through the pastry base
attrs.avoid: Avoid any cracks or holes in the blind-baked pastry; liquid custard will find them.
attrs.fix: After blind baking, check the base for holes and brush with a little beaten egg. Return to the oven for 2 minutes to seal before adding the custard.
